rules.statement: When a script reads a GitHub REST list endpoint (check runs, workflow runs, and the like) whose full result it relies on, page through all results (for example `gh api --paginate --slurp` and merge the item arrays) instead of making one `per_page=100` request.
rules.why: With an unpaged read, items past the first page disappear without warning. Decisions built on the list, such as which checks a ruleset requires, then silently come out incomplete.
rules.check: Look for `gh api` or REST calls to list endpoints with `per_page` and no `--paginate` or page loop, where the code treats the result as the complete set. Don't report it when the code deliberately reads only the newest page and says so.

rules.statement: When a script prints a PowerShell command for the user to copy and run, escape every interpolated value with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.CodeGeneration]::EscapeSingleQuotedStringContent` inside single quotes, quote the script path and invoke it with `&`, and leave out of the command any value the parameter would split, such as a name with a comma in a comma-separated list.
rules.why: PowerShell treats U+2018 to U+201B as single quotes too, so doubling only U+0027 lets a crafted name from an editable workflow file end the string and inject code. An unquoted path with spaces breaks the command, and commas split one value into two.
rules.check: Look for printed or generated command lines that interpolate values or `$PSCommandPath`: escaping done by hand with `-replace "'", "''"`, a script path without quotes, or values containing list separators passed into a list parameter.

rules.statement: In PowerShell, don't give a local or loop variable the same name as a function parameter in any letter case (for example `$name` alongside `[string]$Name`).
rules.why: PowerShell variable names ignore case, so the assignment overwrites the parameter. A later use of the parameter then silently gets the wrong value.
rules.check: Compare the variable names assigned in a function body, especially `foreach` variables and loop assignments, against its `param()` names while ignoring case.

rules.statement: When a script has both a `-WhatIf` (preview) path and an applying path, test the applying path too, and assert on what it actually writes (for example the request bodies a stand-in captured), including per-target results when it runs over several targets.
rules.why: If only the preview is tested, a bug that writes the wrong data, such as reusing one repository's results for another or splitting a name the preview shows intact, passes the suite.
rules.check: For a new or changed feature with `-WhatIf` or `SupportsShouldProcess`, check whether any test runs it without `-WhatIf` and asserts on what was posted or written.

rules.statement: When code sorts items into outcomes, each with its own reason (included, or excluded for reason A or B), give every outcome branch a fixture that reaches it and assert its reason text, and add a fixture for the empty-input case.
rules.why: A branch no fixture reaches, such as a lookup miss or an empty list, can regress, for example by turning into an error or an empty result, without failing any test.
rules.check: List the branches and messages in the sorting code, then check that a test asserts each message and that one fixture supplies an empty list.

rules.statement: When a test stand-in for a paged API serves a list, serve it in several small pages and put some fixture items on a later page, so that code reading only one page fails the tests.
rules.why: A stand-in that returns everything at once can't catch a single-page read that drops items.
rules.check: Look at test fakes for `gh api` or HTTP list endpoints: do they page, and do assertions depend on an item that only a later page holds?
